rubriker.title: Samarkand R6 (open): Uzbekistan beat India to take the sole lead
rubriker._rss_content: Uzbekistan reached the rest day as the sole leaders of the open Chess Olympiad after edging defending champions India 2½–1½ in round six. Nodirbek Yakubboev (pictured) scored the decisive win from what had been an inferior position against Nihal Sarin. China and Armenia moved into joint second on 11/12 match points after beating Germany and Iran, respectively. Uzbekistan, China and Armenia remain unbeaten on individual boards. | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: A Letter From January Complicates FIDE's Account of Israel's Olympiad Forfeits
rubriker._rss_content: Israel's two Olympiad teams had their round six games forfeited this week after a Yom Kippur scheduling request couldn't be resolved with that round's opponents. A letter that's now surfaced, dated eight months before the tournament even began, suggests it never should have come down to that negotiation in the first place.

rubriker.title: Team Israel Forfeits Round 6
rubriker._rss_content: Israel's Open and Women's teams at the Chess Olympiad had their round six games forfeited after a scheduling dispute tied to the observance of Yom Kippur on September 20 and 21 could not be resolved with their opponents.

John Donaldson: New insights into Bobby Fischer
rubriker._rss_content: Bobby Fischer remains one of the most fascinating and enigmatic figures in chess history. IM John Donaldson, captain of the US team at the Chess Olympiad and the author of numerous books on famous and lesser-known chess personalities, is one of the leading experts on Fischer. He recently published a new book on the 1972 World Champion, "Inside the Mind of Bobby Fischer". In the interview, Donaldson talks about his research, previously unknown material and how he views Fischer after years of studying his life and work.

rubriker.title: How can humans prosper in the AI era? Child's play
rubriker._rss_content: Robots solve puzzles more efficiently, but there's a joy derived from unscrambling a Rubik's Cube or mastering chess. This Telegraph article, by Judit Polgar and Erno Rubik, argues that as AI becomes vastly faster and more capable than humans at solving problems, we risk losing something more important than efficiency: the human experience of thinking, experimenting, failing, and discovering.

rubriker._rss_content: Hallingskarvet Sjakklubb i samarbeid med Søråshøgda Sjakklubb arrangerte 18-20. september 2026 sin tredje sjakkfestival på Geilo på bare seks måneder.
